newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National's leaders show true colours - NZ's Cullen.
newsitem.headline: National's leaders show true colours - NZ's Cullen.

text.p: News that the caretaker National party government is prepared to drop its tax cuts to stay in government shows the true colours of that party's leadership, Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen said on Monday.

"We have always suspected National is a party of no core beliefs, no core principles. Now we see the decrepit leadership of the party signalling its preparedness to do anything to hang onto the trappings of power," Cullen said.

The Dominion newspaper's lead story on Monday reported the National Party was considering delaying or ultimately scrapping its second round of tax cuts to accommodate nationalist New Zealand First's demands for increased spending and compulsory superannuation.
The first round of the tax cuts was implemented on July 1, and the second round, which has been legislated for, is due to take effect on July 1, 1997.
NZ First is negotiating with both National and Labour in the bid to form a new government after October's inconclusive general election.
